newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shares close lower for second day.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shares close lower for second day.

text.p: Israeli shares closed lower for the second day on Thursday in what traders said was a much-needed correction.
The benchmark Mishtanim index of the top 100 shares fell 0.43 percent, or 1.05 points, to 240.59 on all-share turnover of 116 million shekels against 145 million shekels on Wednesday.
The Maof 25 blue chip index closed 0.65 percent lower at 249.35.
"A consolidation is natural after the market's rapid rise. We want to see a much stronger correction before the market resumes its rise," said Danni Scharia of Capital Securities.

"All the technical indicators support a correction. The sharp rise of the market is frightening. The best thing would be for the Maof to stabilise at 245 before it starts rising again," Scharia added.

"The recent rise is unsustainable and the market needs to find an equilibrium point. Share prices are high but there is a general consensus that the market will stabilise at the current level," said Baruch Glicksberg of Clal Insurance.
Elite Industries rose 1.0 percent to 7,759 agorot. Elite was rated a "strong buy" in a report released on Thursday by Societe Generale Equities and Derivatives.
The brokerage house said that by 1998 earnings are expected to have more than doubled, placing the share price on a forward multiple of around 8.0.

Osem Investments closed unchanged at 1,901 agorot. Societe Generale rated the company a buy, saying it expected little growth in 1996 earnings, but forecast increases of 16 percent in 1997 and 36 percent in 1998, placing the stock on a forward multiple of 11.5.
The most active share was Israel Chemicals, which closed unchanged at 352 agorot on turnover of 7.5 million shekels.

The number two most active was Teva Pharmaceutical Industries, which surged 3.25 percent to 1,876 on volume of seven million shekels. Teva's American depositary receipts, which are traded on Nasdaq, rose two percent on Wednesday on high turnover of $60 million.
The number three most active was Delek the Israel Fuel Corp, which gained 0.5 percent to 8,969. Traders said they did not know why the stock traded so actively today.
